model.name: Administrative Area
model.purpose: Represent a governed administrative or official statistical territorial unit with stable identity, versioned codes and names, authority, hierarchy, direct boundary geometry and lifecycle independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns administrative-area identity, type and level, code and name bindings, constitutive authority references, typed hierarchy, source-qualified boundaries, CRS, topology, effective time, lifecycle, recognition and provenance. Governments, jurisdictions, instruments, settlements, addresses, zones, parcels, terrain, statistics and disputes remain external masters.
in_scope: Unit identity, code systems, names, class, level, authority and instruments
Administrative and spatial hierarchy, boundary roles, geometry, CRS, area, topology and quality
Lifecycle and lineage, place and statistic references, disputes, projections and safe operations
out_of_scope: Government organization, legal jurisdiction and sovereignty adjudication
Settlement, address, postal, electoral, service and planning zones, parcel, terrain and population masters
Universal recognition of codes, boundaries or territorial claims

boundary_notes.distinction: A government is an organization and a jurisdiction is a competence relation; the administrative area is the territorial unit they may govern.
A settlement or locality can cross or sit within units, and addresses locate objects; none defines administrative identity.
These purpose-built zones can map to administrative units but retain independent authority, geometry and lifecycle.
A parcel is a land-administration spatial unit at property or cadastral grain, not an administrative government territory.
The model preserves who claims or recognizes an extent and for what scope but never decides universal sovereignty.

sources.title: Standard country or area codes for statistical use, M49
sources.version_or_date: UN M49 methodology and current list, accessed 6 September 2026
sources.relevance: Provides numerical country and area codes and geographic-region groupings for statistical use, including change history and explicit statistical purpose.

sources.title: INSPIRE Data Specification on Administrative Units
sources.version_or_date: Technical Guidelines, current document service accessed 6 September 2026
sources.relevance: Defines administrative units, boundaries, levels, national codes, names, residence of authority and lifecycle metadata for European spatial-data interoperability.

sources.title: OGC GeoSPARQL 1.1
sources.relevance: Defines feature and geometry representations, coordinate reference system serialization and topological relations for semantic spatial projections.

sources.title: Geography Markup Language
sources.relevance: Provides feature, geometry, coordinate reference system, topology and temporal encodings used by administrative-boundary exchange profiles.

sources.title: ISO 19112 Geographic information, Spatial referencing by geographic identifiers
sources.relevance: Provides a conceptual scheme for spatial references based on geographic identifiers and gazetteer relationships, useful for code and name based location without equating identifiers with geometry.

sources.title: Regulation on the establishment of a common classification of territorial units for statistics
sources.relevance: Establishes NUTS territorial units for statistics and amendment cycles; these statistical units are not automatically equivalent to administrative or legal jurisdictions.

sources.title: Second Administrative Level Boundaries
sources.relevance: Provides a UN-supported repository and methodology for first and second subnational administrative boundaries and their temporal changes, with national-source and validation context.

sources.title: The GeoJSON Format
sources.relevance: Defines a WGS 84 web geometry encoding and antimeridian rules; it is a display or exchange projection and cannot preserve every native CRS, topology or disputed-boundary semantic.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines timestamps with seconds and explicit UTC relation for legal-effect, observation, publication, knowledge and lifecycle events.

composition.target: Government, Jurisdiction, Instrument, Place, Address, Zone, Parcel, Statistic and Dispute models
composition.purpose: Connect administrative territory to external legal, organizational, spatial, observational and dispute masters.
Bind versioned country or subdivision codes and geographic-identifier schemes without replacing the master identity.
Project statistical area codes and time-aware first or second administrative boundary references.
Project European administrative and statistical unit identifiers, levels, names, geometry and lifecycle.
Publish geometry and semantic-spatial views with CRS, topology, dispute and mapping-loss declarations.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension identity, owner, administrative-register authority, boundary steward and namespace
Area, government, instrument, code-list, boundary, place, zone, statistic, dispute and lifecycle registries
Master-system mappings for area, code, hierarchy, boundary assertion, change case and event identifiers
Code, naming, hierarchy, CRS, topology, recognition, dispute, access, retention and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint administrative-area and assertion identifiers only when no authoritative register identity exists; keep governments, instruments, settlements, addresses, postal and electoral zones, parcels, statistics and disputes as typed references.
registry_links: Dimension-local area, code, name, hierarchy, boundary, lineage and recognition registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative administrative-unit identifier and register, never by name, ISO or statistical code, parent, government, geometry, population, date or hash.
Keep administrative hierarchy, geometric containment, statistical grouping, jurisdiction and governmental competence distinct.
patch_rules: Extensions declare unit profile, target finding, source, authority, code-list versions, CRS, recognition scope and interoperability impact.
Identity, authority, hierarchy, boundary, legal-effect or lifecycle semantic changes require a successor version, migration map and continued resolution of prior records.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when identity, codes, unit class, authority, hierarchy type, boundary role, CRS, legal effect, recognition and lineage remain intact.
Every code, hierarchy and geometry projection pins versions and states transformation, omission and round-trip limits.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for the administrative unit, qualified by register and issuing authority.
Governed globally resolvable area IRI with authoritative register binding.
Dimension UUID or ULID when no external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and offset or Z; separate decision, legal-effect, observation, publication, knowledge and ingestion times.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {area-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use a name, code, geometry, date or hash alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, issuer, source and profile versions, CRS, authority, recognition scope, valid and knowledge times, quality, licence and access marking.

policies: Only a competent register authority may create or change canonical administrative-unit identity and legal-effect state.
Code, name, geometry, population, postal coverage and government seat never alone prove current administrative identity or authority.
Official, statistical, claimed, disputed and de facto boundary assertions remain separately attributable.
Agents may validate and propose; legal change, universal-recognition claims, dispute suppression and wider disclosure require accountable authority.

read: Resolve Dimension, register, purpose, code editions, hierarchy type, valid and knowledge time, boundary role, CRS and recognition scope.
create: Create identity, authority, unit class, instrument, state, source and explicit unknowns before codes, hierarchy or geometry.
update: Append assertion or event with authority, reason, time, evidence and validation; never overwrite cited history or competing claims.
delete: Apply legal hold and retention; prefer abolition or tombstone and never cascade to governments, places, statistics or disputes.

roles.name: Administrative-register authority
responsibilities: Own canonical unit identity, class, hierarchy and legal-effect lifecycle.

roles.name: Boundary authority
responsibilities: Provide authoritative geometry, demarcation and quality evidence.

roles.name: Code-list authority
responsibilities: Issue versioned codes and preserve retired-code mappings.

roles.name: Statistical authority
responsibilities: Own statistical groupings, observations, reference geographies and methods.

roles.name: Recognition and dispute steward
responsibilities: Preserve claims, recognition scope and neutral-display rules without erasure.

roles.name: Geospatial quality steward
responsibilities: Validate CRS, topology, transformations and measures.

roles.name: Access and records steward
responsibilities: Apply disclosure, licence, retention and audit policy.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and sensitive boundary or authority disclosure unless register, role, purpose and field policy grant it; expose the minimum necessary precision and claim context.
exceptions: Statutory, judicial, humanitarian or emergency access cites authority and remains purpose-bound, attributable and reviewable.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, area, action, policy, RFC 3339 time, authority, recognition scope, affected fields and outcome.

read_order: Read Dimension area-register, code, hierarchy, boundary, CRS, recognition, dispute, access and retention policies.
Read this model and linked government, instrument, place, zone, parcel, statistic and dispute models before mutation.

coverage.claim: A source-grounded reviewable draft of an administrative area across ISO 3166 and ISO 19112, UN M49 and SALB, INSPIRE Administrative Units, NUTS, OGC GeoSPARQL and GML, GeoJSON and RFC 3339, without universal sovereignty, jurisdictional legal-effect or certified crosswalk claims.

checklist.notes: Register-qualified identity, code bindings, unit class and names are explicit.
Administrative and statistical types, levels and schemes are versioned.
Names, codes, hierarchy, boundary geometry, CRS, area and topology are first-class.
Official, statistical, claimed, disputed and de facto sources and confidence are covered.
Register, name, code, bind, map, change, dispute, project and retire operations are governed.
Governments, laws, places, zones, parcels, statistics and disputes retain external masters.
Creation, split, merger, transfer, annexation, renaming, recoding, reclassification and abolition preserve history.
Administrative parentage, spatial containment, statistical grouping and competence are distinct.
Decision, legal-effect, observation, publication, knowledge and ingestion times remain distinct.
Boundary roles, CRS, dimensionality, accuracy, topology, enclaves and exclaves are covered.
Authorities, instruments, code lists, geometry sources, transformations and claims remain attributable.
Register, boundary, code, government, statistical and dispute masters remain separate.
Identity, code, hierarchy cycles, CRS, topology, legal time, lineage and stale-head checks are explicit.
Purpose views, dispute sensitivity, coordinate precision and inference risk are covered.
Historic codes, names, geometries, disputes, successor lineage and tombstones are preserved.
ISO 3166, UN M49, NUTS, SALB, INSPIRE, GML, GeoSPARQL and GeoJSON are loss-aware.

known_omissions: No independent Claude or Grok result was available; later administrative, geopolitical and geospatial review is required before canonical promotion.
Jurisdiction-specific local-government law, sovereignty, indigenous and customary territory, maritime, condominium, historical and conflict-sensitive profiles require specialist review.
The frozen relation ledger contains no approved WM-PLC-004 rows; composition targets remain draft.
Certified ISO, M49, NUTS, SALB, INSPIRE, GML, GeoSPARQL and GeoJSON crosswalks and conformance fixtures remain future work.
conflicts: Administrative hierarchy, geometric containment, statistical grouping and governmental jurisdiction may disagree.
Official, claimed, disputed, de facto and statistical boundaries may all be legitimate assertions for different purposes.
A rename or recode may preserve identity in one jurisdiction while a reclassification or transfer may create a successor in another.
regional_assumptions: INSPIRE and NUTS are European profiles and do not define universal administrative law.
ISO 3166 and UN M49 provide code and statistical schemes and do not settle sovereignty or boundary disputes.
SALB and geospatial standards support exchange but do not create legal effect for a national register.
adversarial_checks: Reject identity from a name, ISO code, map polygon or government name alone.
Reject hierarchy inferred from geometry containment or statistical grouping without explicit relation type.
Reject a disputed or de facto line represented as universally recognized official boundary.
Reject lifecycle change without instrument, authority, effective time and predecessor-successor mapping.
Reject agent legal change, dispute suppression or universal-recognition claim without accountable confirmation.
